title: Isa in the Qur'an's telling
hook: the Qur'an says Isa was not killed but raised to Allah, and calls him a word and a spirit from Him (4:157–158; 4:171)

segments.voice: Yesterday, sulh: and reconciliation is better. Your line was reconciliation is better. Did you let go of one thing for the sake of peace? Day three hundred eighty-seven, and the last day of an-Nisa.

Jesus, in Arabic, is Isa. Some people meet him in the Qur'an for the first time and are surprised at what they find. The Qur'an calls him the Messiah, al-Masih. His mother Maryam has a surah named for her. Muslims say peace be upon him after his name, as they do for the other prophets. Near the end of an-Nisa, two short passages give the Qur'an's own account of who he was, and of how his life on earth ended.
screen: `ISA, THE SON OF MARYAM.` → `AL-MASIH, THE MESSIAH.` → `TWO SHORT PASSAGES.`

segments.voice: The first passage, 4:157, answers a claim made by some in his day, that they had killed the Messiah. In Pickthall's words: "They slew him not nor crucified him, but it appeared so unto them." And 4:158: God raised him up to Himself. The common Muslim reading is that Isa was not crucified, and that God took him up alive. How it appeared so has been explained in different ways. One classical explanation is that someone else was made to look like him. Other commentators said only that the matter was made to seem so, without naming how. Some Muslim thinkers have read the verse differently again. And hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari speak of Isa returning before the end of time. Christians, for their part, believe Jesus was crucified, died, and rose again, and that event is at the center of their faith. Here the two traditions differ plainly, and each holds its account with deep conviction. The second passage, 4:171, says who Isa is. In Pickthall's words: "The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, was only a messenger of Allah, and His word which He conveyed unto Mary, and a spirit from Him." A word, kalimah. Muslims commonly explain it by 3:59: like Adam, he was created by God's word, be, and he was. A spirit from Him, ruh minhu. The same verse asks the People of the Scripture not to say three, and Christians, who understand the Trinity as one God, have long discussed this verse with Muslims. Both traditions call him the Messiah. Both call him a word. They mean different things by it, and it's worth knowing exactly what each one means.
screen: `THEY SLEW HIM NOT, IN THE QUR'AN'S TELLING` · `RAISED UP TO GOD` · `WHERE THE TWO TRADITIONS DIFFER` · `KALIMAH: A WORD; RUH: A SPIRIT` · then, large: `HIS WORD WHICH HE CONVEYED UNTO MARY.`

segments.voice: Today's practice is reading, slowly. After the session, read 4:157 to 159 and 4:171 in a translation you trust, once, without hurrying. For now, when the bell starts, sit with the two phrases: a word from Him, a spirit from Him. Don't try to settle anything. Just notice what it means that a person can be called a word. If you have Christian friends, notice too that they hold him in deep love, in their own way. Let both facts sit in the same quiet. The bell holds the time.
Isa in the Qur'an's telling. A messenger, the Messiah, a word from God conveyed to Maryam, and a spirit from Him, raised up to God. Today's word.
screen: `ISA IN THE QUR'AN'S TELLING — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: a word from him. Today, read the verses once, slowly, and if it comes up with someone of another faith, listen to what they believe before you explain what you do. Day three hundred eighty-seven.

howItsDone: Muslims honor Isa as a prophet and the Messiah, born of the virgin Maryam; the common Muslim reading of 4:157–158 is that he was not crucified but raised alive to God, hadith speak of his return before the end of time, and Muslims say 'peace be upon him' after his name.

fork.setup: 4:171 describes Isa in three ways. which list is it?
options: a teacher, a healer, a king.
a messenger of God, His word conveyed to Maryam, and a spirit from Him.
an angel, a sign, a mystery.
fork.reveal: messenger, word and spirit. Muslims commonly read 'word' through 3:59: created like Adam, by God's word, be.

trapdoor: what you thought: Islam doesn't talk about Jesus.
what it means: the Qur'an calls Isa the Messiah, a messenger, a word and a spirit from God, and says he was raised up to God.
what a scholar hears: shubbiha lahum, 'it was made to appear so to them', read in several ways; kalimah explained by 3:59; and the return of Isa in the hadith literature.
